nodes.label: Temperature Scheduling for Open Set Recognition
nodes.rationale: Proposes novel temperature schedules (T_NegCosSch, T_CosSch) that improve OSR performance by starting with lower temperature and moving to higher temperature, making tighter representation clusters for closed set classes while keeping open set examples distant.

nodes.label: Open Set Recognition Problem
nodes.rationale: Core problem: classifying known classes while detecting unknown classes. Addressed through representation learning and loss function design.

nodes.label: OSR Loss Functions (CE, SupCon, ARPL)
nodes.rationale: Three main loss functions analyzed: Cross-Entropy (CE), Supervised Contrastive (SupCon), and Adversarial Reciprocal Points Learning (ARPL). Temperature scaling affects gradient behavior differently in each.

nodes.label: OSR Benchmarks (CIFAR, TinyImageNet, CUB, Aircraft, SCars)
nodes.rationale: Standard benchmarks for evaluating OSR methods with known-unknown splits and semantic shift benchmarks (SSBs).

nodes.label: Temperature Scaling in Neural Networks
nodes.rationale: Temperature τ in softmax controls sharpness of probability distributions. Small τ amplifies logit differences (sharper); large τ smooths them. Used in knowledge distillation, calibration, contrastive learning.

nodes.label: Representation Learning for Open Set Recognition
nodes.rationale: Core OSR approach: learn representations where known classes cluster tightly and unknown classes remain distant. Temperature scheduling affects representation geometry during training.

nodes.label: Boosting Open Set Recognition Performance through Modulated Representation Learning
nodes.author: Amit Kumar Kundu, Vaishnavi S Patil, Joseph Jaja
nodes.rationale: Proposes temperature-modulated representation learning via novel negative cosine schedule (NegCosSch) to improve open set recognition by balancing instance-level and semantic-level features without computational overhead.

nodes.label: Temperature Scheduling for Representation Learning
nodes.rationale: Dynamic temperature modulation during training enabling gradual task switching from instance-specific to semantic features, creating richer and more generalizable representation spaces for both open and closed set tasks.

nodes.label: Negative Cosine Schedule (NegCosSch)
nodes.rationale: Novel temperature schedule starting with lower temperature for coarse decision boundary, gradually increasing to prioritize more neighbors and refine representations while maintaining separation from open set samples.

nodes.label: Open Set Recognition (OSR)
nodes.rationale: Task of simultaneously classifying known classes and detecting unknown classes not present in training data, requiring strong generalization and ability to discern novel semantic classes.

nodes.label: Semantic Shift Benchmarks (SSBs)
nodes.rationale: Fine-grained OSR benchmarks on CUB, FGVC-Aircraft, and Stanford Cars with varying difficulty levels and more training classes, providing more challenging evaluation than standard OSR benchmarks.

nodes.label: Temperature Effect on Representation Learning
nodes.rationale: Lower temperature encourages instance-specific features with sharp decision boundaries; higher temperature encourages semantic features with smooth boundaries—fixed temperature prevents exploring both ends of spectrum.

nodes.label: Cross-Entropy Loss
nodes.rationale: Standard classification loss where temperature parameter scales logits before softmax, controlling sharpness of probability distributions.

nodes.label: Supervised Contrastive Loss (SupCon)
nodes.rationale: Loss function using multi-viewed batches to push apart negative samples and pull together positive samples, with temperature controlling hard negative mining.

nodes.label: ARPL Loss
nodes.rationale: OSR-specific loss function by Chen et al. (2021) that can be enhanced with temperature scheduling for improved performance.

nodes.label: Familiarity Hypothesis
nodes.rationale: Hypothesis by Dietterich & Guyer (2022) that OSR methods detect novelty from absence of learned semantic features, recommending extraction of instance-level features for improved detection.

nodes.label: Label Smoothing
nodes.rationale: Regularization technique softening one-hot labels; can provide additional performance improvements when combined with temperature scheduling.

nodes.label: Maximum Logit Scoring Rule
nodes.rationale: OSR scoring rule using maximum logit value to distinguish known from unknown classes; foundation for evaluating OSR performance.

nodes.label: AUROC Metric
nodes.rationale: Area under receiver operating characteristic curve measuring known-unknown detection performance in OSR.

nodes.label: Open Set Classification Rate (OSCR)
nodes.rationale: Metric measuring trade-off between open set and closed set performance in OSR tasks.

hyperedges.label: OSR Temperature Scheduling System
hyperedges.rationale: Integrated approach: temperature schedules modify loss function behavior to improve representation learning for OSR, evaluated on standard benchmarks. Temperature scheduling is the novel contribution that ties together loss design and representation geometry.
